paper:
Amina Belkacem is a fifteen-year-old pupil from Sétif. Last year, she noticed that her grandmother often forgot to take her medicine. So, she decided to invent a smart pill box. The box rings and lights up when it is time to take a pill, and it sends a message to the family's phone if the pill is not taken.

Amina worked on her project for six months with the help of her physics teacher. She used a small electronic card, a speaker and a battery. Her invention was presented at the national science fair in Algiers, and it won the first prize. Since then, she has received many invitations from universities and companies.

"I want to become an engineer and help old people live safely," she says. "Science is not only in books; it is in our daily life."

(Text written by the site)

Part One (14 points)

A. Reading comprehension (7 points)

1. True or false? a) Amina's grandmother forgot to take her medicine. b) Amina worked alone. c) Her invention won the first prize.

2. Answer: a) What does the pill box do when the pill is not taken? b) What does Amina want to become?

3. Who or what do the underlined words refer to? "her" (§1, line 2) → … ; "it" (§2, line 3) → …

B. Mastery of language (7 points)

1. Find in the text words closest in meaning to: clever = … ; got = …

2. Find in the text the opposite of: dangerously ≠ … ; young ≠ …

3. Put the verbs between brackets in the correct tense: Amina (to start) her project last year. She (to win) three prizes since then.

4. Turn into the passive: The jury chose the best invention.

5. Classify according to the pronunciation of final "s": pills – lights – boxes – books
